statements.text: Even though President Trump already forced through the largest cut to health care in our nation’s history with the Big Ugly Law, the Administration is once again attacking lifesaving care – this time by adding prior authorization requirements to Medicare. Under this new program, private companies can use artificial intelligence, rather than medical expertise, to conduct private screenings and determine whether patients should receive coverage for dozens of procedures. Delaying and denying care is never the answer.

Accidentally matching with my good friend and partner, @katiefryhester! As Congress looks to regulate AI and other emerging technologies, we must continue to work with our state partners who are actively delivering solutions and tackling these issues. I sat down with Senator Hester to discuss how I can best support the bipartisan work of the Maryland General Assembly to address the impacts of AI in classrooms, workplaces, health care systems, and local communities here in Congress.
Unfettered sale of LNG to countries like China and Russia would power their data centers, AI systems, and cyber missions, all by using American energy.

statements.text: The rapid development of AI threatens to outpace our ability to counter cyber threats to our nation's security. Our national security leaders – many of whom fight these global threats from CYBERCOMM headquarters at Fort Meade here in Maryland – must maintain the education and expertise to utilize rapidly developing technologies. I'm grateful to work with Representative Larsen to develop an AI strategy for our servicemembers.
statements.venue: Press release on AI Training for National Security Act included in FY26 NDAA

statements.text: Almost 20 years ago in the Odenton Library, a few committed individuals came together to build the Fort Meade Alliance – and that alliance continues to support the economic growth and national security interests of Fort Meade and the region to this day. As the only Marylander on a defense or national security committee, I joined President of the Fort Meade Alliance, Roxanne Wood, and Corporate Vice President and President of Northrop Grumman Mission Systems, Roshan Roeder to provide an update from Washington, discuss the impacts of AI on our workforce, ongoing challenges at our installations, and what excites us most about Fort Meade’s future. Thank you to Tim O’Ferrall, General Manager of the Fort Meade Alliance for organizing!

It’s never too early to be civically engaged, and the incredible Howard County high schoolers interning with my friend @katiefryhester are perfect examples of that! I sat down with these students to hear about everything they're working on, including AI regulation policy, and how I can support that work in Washington. There’s no one better to hear from on challenges of the future than the next generation leaders.

7 in 10 Americans oppose the construction of AI data centers in their communities – but as AI takes off, many of our neighbors are asking: What the heck is Congress actually doing about data centers? That’s today’s topic of Sarah Explains It All! https://t.co/z5SBVSWvG7

Congress cannot afford to miss the moment on AI regulation. While reasonable people may disagree on how precisely to regulate this technology, we are beyond denying that action is required. Speaker Johnson plans to send us home on Thursday for seven weeks – without even an attempt to pass any meaningful, bipartisan AI safeguards. It’s unacceptable.

https://t.co/8GaV3lbZc3

Congress has an obligation to those we serve to tackle the most urgent and complex problems facing our nation and world. Instead of doing that with AI, the Speaker canceled votes and sent us home two weeks early. That’s why I've joined @RepLiccardo in urging Speaker Johnson to reconvene the House and advance meaningful, bipartisan AI safeguards. AI isn’t slowing down, and neither should Congress. We need to be here in Washington, working towards meaningful regulations for this technology – it’s what our constituents elected us to do.

As AI continues to rapidly evolve, we need regulations at home and abroad. I’ve joined @RepYassAnsari and over 40 of my House Democratic colleagues in urging the Trump Administration to establish a coordinated global framework with our allies to regulate AI development. Especially as we grapple with the uncertainty of these advancements, it’s all the more important to work with our longstanding allies to ensure true global security.

NEW: The Trump Administration is considering handing over 17,000+ acres of public land across six states to build dozens of new data centers. Over the past 21 months, we’ve seen unprecedented attempts by this Administration to politicize, privatize, and profit off of our public lands – and this is no exception. That’s why I’ve joined @RepHuffman in demanding answers from Secretary Burgum on these reported plans to cede our public lands for massive data center projects because these spaces belong to the people, not AI executives.

We cannot afford to miss the mark on AI safety and oversight. The Center for AI Standards and Innovation, or CAISI, is the key government office that evaluates AI systems and coordinates oversight at the federal level. With the rapidly emerging capabilities in AI, this office is currently too underresourced and underfunded to meet the moment. That’s why I’ve joined @BradSherman and my colleagues in urging an increase in funding for this crucial agency.

Reason number 7,849 (or infinity) the Speaker needs to bring Congress back NOW and regulate AI.
